Compute composite scores on test set based on previous cell groups

compute.test.set.Rd

Scores the cell groups learned on a training set in an independent (test) set, on the same scale as the training scores. Three steps:

  1. the training deconvolution subgroups are rebuilt in the test data with multideconv::replicate_deconvolution_subgroups() (each subgroup is the median of its member features);

  2. for each cell group, its features are scaled with the training means and standard deviations;

  3. they are projected with the training CCA weights of the cell group, giving one score per test sample.

Scoring the training samples themselves reproduces their training scores. Each test sample is scored on its own, so a single sample can be scored (except for cell groups built with batch, see Details).

Usage

compute.test.set(dt, cell_groups, group_names = NULL, deconv_test)

Arguments

dt

Deconvolution subgroups of the training set, as returned by multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis() (the elements Deconvolution matrix and Deconvolution subgroups composition are used).

cell_groups

The cell groups of the training set, as returned by construct_cell_groups(): its elements Composition (features of each cell group) and Weights (CCA projection parameters xcoef, train_means, train_sds of each cell group) are used. Older unnamed lists, with these as second and third elements, are also accepted.

group_names

Optional character vector with the names of the cell groups to score. If NULL (default), all cell groups are scored. Names that are not cell groups are ignored with a message; an error is raised if none of them is a cell group.

deconv_test

A data frame or matrix with the deconvolution features of the test set before subgrouping (the same kind of matrix as given to multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis() for the training set, with the same column names), samples as rows.

Value

A data frame with one row per test sample (sample names as row names) and one column per scored cell group, on the scale of the training scores. A cell group is scored only if all its features are in the test set without missing values: a score computed from part of them can be very different from the training score (even reversed), so the other cell groups are skipped, with a warning listing them. An error is raised if no cell group can be scored.

Details

If the cell groups were built with batch correction (batch in construct_cell_groups()), the features of the test samples are z-scored on their own means and SDs (as each training cohort was), so deconv_test should contain a single cohort with several samples: the scores then describe each sample relative to the other test samples. A warning is given when such cell groups are scored with fewer than 10 test samples.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
data("deconv.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)

#> 44 of 897 features were not assigned to any cluster by the tree cut and are not part of any cell group (pink: 2, yellow: 8, red: 2, blue: 6, brown: 4, turquoise: 12, black: 4, green: 6)
test_scores <- compute.test.set(deconv_subgroups.tuto, cell_groups,
                                deconv_test = deconv.tuto[1:20, ])
test_scores[1:3, 1:3]
